title: RBI Prohibits NDF Contracts in Rupee & Caps Banks' Net Open Position at $100M
summary: RBI tightens forex regulations to curb rupee volatility, banning banks from offering non-deliverable forward (NDF) contracts in INR.

blocks.title: 📰 2. 🏛️ REGULATORY BODIES NEWS
blocks.text: 🪝 RBI Prohibits NDF Contracts in Rupee & Caps Banks' Net Open Position at $100M. Key development for Banking & General Awareness.

items: The Reserve Bank of India prohibited banks from offering Non-Deliverable Forward (NDF) contracts in the Indian Rupee to both resident and non-resident clients, following a ~10% decline in INR during FY26.
**Net Open Position (NOP) Cap**: Onshore deliverable NOP capped at **$100 million per bank** at the end of each business day (down from 25% of capital).
**Related-Party Derivative Exemption**: Eased rules allowing back-to-back genuine risk-offsetting trades across overseas branches while maintaining the $100M NOP cap.
🎯 Exam Angle → Focus on statutory circular guidelines, compliance deadlines, penal provisions, and applicability thresholds across scheduled banks.
